memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to examine the sore on the skin, and if the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore appears to be more than skin deep, it is a defiling skin disease. When the priest examines that person, he shall pronounce them ceremonially unclean." - Lev 13:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two signs told the priest this was serious. The hair had turned white, and the sore went deeper than the surface.

That second phrase is the one to hold on to: more than skin deep. Anyone can have a mark on the skin. The question was whether it had gone down into something.

We are not good at this kind of examination in our own lives. We look at the surface. Is anyone upset with me? Does my life look respectable? Am I still turning up on Sunday? But God has never assessed us at surface level. He told Samuel plainly: people look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart (1 Sam 16:7).

A sharp tone with our children is surface. What lies underneath — exhaustion, resentment, a fear we have not named — is the real matter. An hour lost to a screen is surface. The emptiness we are trying not to feel is deeper.

The writer of Hebrews says the word of God is living and active, sharper than any double-edged sword, penetrating to divide soul and spirit, judging the thoughts and attitudes of the heart (Heb 4:12). That sounds frightening until we remember who wields it. It is a Physician's blade, not an executioner's.

Let Him look deeper than skin.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What surface behaviour in your life might have something deeper underneath it?
2. Are you willing to let God examine below the level you are comfortable with?
3. What would it mean to invite God's Word to search you this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see beneath the surface of my life. Do not let me settle for looking respectable. Search me, show me what lies underneath, and heal me at the root. Amen.
